sources.entry: Agenta - LLMOps platform for prompt management, LLM evaluation, and observability. Build, evaluate, and monitor production-grade LLM applications with collaborative prompt engineering. (Source Code) MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: Agenta is an open-source, self-hostable workspace where teams build chat-driven AI agents, share them, and run them from Slack, Telegram, WhatsApp, or the web app.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Agenta as a workspace for building specialized agents by chatting with them, describing the work, connecting apps, and improving agents through feedback. Agents can be used in the web app or in Slack, Telegram, or WhatsApp Business. Automations let agents run on a schedule or when an event occurs in a connected app, with a history of each run. Integrations are offered via MCP and through Composio (more than 1,000 apps, including Gmail, Slack, Notion, and GitHub). Permissions can be set per agent for tools, and every run is traced and every cost tracked. Model choice includes hosted APIs or self-hosted models via Ollama. The README positions Agenta as different from coding agents, single-user assistants, and low-code workflow builders.
use_cases: Build shared AI agents for a team by chatting
Automate recurring work on a schedule or from app events
Run agents from Slack, Telegram, or WhatsApp
Track agent runs, versions, and model costs
Self-host an agent workspace on your own models and data
Set per-agent tool permissions with human approval
how_to_run: Self-host by pasting into an agent: npx skills add Agenta-AI/agenta-skills
Then ask the agent to help self-host Agenta with its repository
See the self-hosting documentation for details
notable: Agents are built by chatting rather than drawing workflows
Per-agent permissions control which tools an agent can use and whether it can read or write
Each session runs in its own sandbox, and model credentials are not visible to the agent
Every run is traced and every cost tracked
Agents can call other agents and hand off work
caveats: The README does not give detailed hardware or infrastructure requirements for self-hosting
Some features (such as Composio connections and chat-app integrations) depend on external services
A managed Agenta Cloud option is also offered; its pricing is not stated in the README
keywords: run ai agents on my own servers
share ai assistant with my team
